language_wrapper: Consider the polynomial P(x) = product_{i=1}^{n} (1 - r^i x)(1 + r^i x). Let C be the coefficient of x^(2{t}) in P(x). Compute the absolute value |C|.
hardness_rationale: The seed problem only requires the coefficient of x^2 from a linear product with simple alternating signs, reducible via basic symmetric sums: C = (S^2 - sum a_i^2)/2. Our family asks for the coefficient of x^(2t) in a product of paired geometric factors (1 - r^i x)(1 + r^i x) over i = 1..n. This collapses to ∏(1 - r^{2i} x^2) and demands recognition of the q-binomial (Gaussian binomial) identity: ∏_{i=1}^n (1 - q^i y) = Σ_{t=0}^n (-1)^t q^{t(t+1)/2} [n choose t]_q y^t. Extracting the coefficient thus involves nontrivial manipulation with q-analogs, far beyond the seed’s elementary symmetric-sum trick. The verifier enforces t ≥ 2 and r ≥ 2 to avoid trivial zero/linear cases, ensuring instances require this advanced approach and cannot be solved by simple guessing or low-degree identities.
notes: Implementation relies on the exact integer nature of Gaussian binomial coefficients via the product formula. Bounds keep outputs within practical ranges while still sizable. The absolute value removes sign ambiguity from (-1)^t.
source_question: Let $C$ be the coefficient of $x^2$ in the expansion of the product $(1 - x)(1 + 2x)(1 - 3x)\cdots(1 + 14x)(1 - 15x).$ Find $|C|.$
